title: Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 8 – Resource Management
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 8, organised by its three Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
course: NSW Earth and Environmental Science Stage 6
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How are Australia’s resources extracted, used & managed?

questions.prompt: What type of resource can be naturally replenished on a human timescale?
What type of resource exists in finite amounts or forms too slowly to replace quickly?
What large Australian groundwater resource underlies much of inland eastern Australia?
What mining method removes a large surface pit to access near-surface ore?
What mining method accesses deep resources through shafts and tunnels?
What process repairs land after mining to restore environmental function?
What group should be involved when mining or rehabilitation may affect Aboriginal cultural sites and Country?
questions.answer: Traditional Owners. Accept: Aboriginal Traditional Owners.

questions.prompt: What industry farms aquatic organisms such as fish, oysters or prawns?
What waste strategy means avoiding the creation of waste in the first place?
questions.answer: Reduce. Accept: avoidance or waste reduction.

questions.prompt: What strategy uses an item again without turning it into a new material?
What strategy processes waste materials into new products?
What process turns organic waste into a nutrient-rich soil-like material?
What engineered site is used for the disposal of solid waste in the ground?
What gas produced by decomposing organic waste in landfills can be captured for energy?
What liquid formed when water passes through waste and carries dissolved contaminants is called?
What approach ranks waste options from most to least preferred, beginning with avoidance and reduction?

categories.name: How can natural resources be managed sustainably?

questions.prompt: What term means meeting present needs without compromising future generations?
What activity removes organisms or resources faster than they can be naturally replaced?
What environmental impact results when vegetation or ecosystems are cleared for human use?
What type of pollution can reduce the sustainability of rivers, lakes and groundwater?
What Aboriginal land-management practice uses carefully controlled fire to care for Country?
What broad area of responsibility involves caring for Country through cultural knowledge and practices?
questions.answer: Caring for Country. Accept: Indigenous land management.

questions.prompt: What three broad dimensions are commonly balanced in sustainability decisions?
What term describes the benefits people obtain from healthy ecosystems, such as clean water and pollination?

finalRound.prompt: What management principle aims to meet current needs while preserving resources and environmental function for future generations?
